# Notes of this project for coding agents

Repo Pager: A Telegram bot on a Cloudflare Worker that tells its maintainer only what needs them in their GitHub repositories, and acts on it with a button.

This file belongs to the project: the blueprint wrote it once, and its updates leave it alone. It adds to `AGENTS.md` what a coding agent needs to know about this project alone, such as its architecture, the commands of its own checks and what to watch for in its tests.

## Where things are

- Repo Pager is self-hosted: everyone runs an instance of their own, and there is no shared app ([decision 0018](../docs/decisions/0018-the-pager-is-repo-pager-which-everyone-runs-as-an-instance-of-their-own.md)). `wrangler.jsonc` holds the values of the maintainer's own instance: never change `name`, `dennis-otto-pager`, the name of his Worker, whose secrets and Durable Object state belong to it, nor the id of its namespace of Workers KV. Docs, code and tests speak of *the maintainer* and of Repo Pager, never of one person, and the guide names a control repository and a Worker of the reader's own.
- The Worker is in `src/`, with its handlers in `src/index.ts`, its metadata and version in `package.json`, and its name, bindings and compatibility date in `wrangler.jsonc`; Cloudflare builds and deploys it with Workers Builds, as `docs/releases.md` describes, and its secrets live in Cloudflare, never in the repository.
- `README.md` documents installation, configuration and use, `docs/` holds the pages of the website, and `CHANGELOG.md` lists the changes of every release.
- The tests are in `test/`; `scripts/check.sh` runs every check.

## The parts of the pager

- `src/index.ts` has the three routes and the schedule; each request proves where it comes from first (`src/crypto.ts`), and `src/settings.ts` reads the variables of `wrangler.jsonc` and the secrets, which live in Cloudflare.
- `src/rules.ts` is the one place that decides what counts: add or change a rule there, with its test in `test/rules.test.ts`, and keep `docs/how-it-works.md` and its German page in step. `github-app.json`, the manifest of the GitHub App, subscribes to exactly the events that the rules read, as `test/manifest.test.ts` checks.
- `src/buttons.ts` is the allowlist of the buttons per kind and state; `src/actions.ts` runs them. A new action takes an entry in both, a test of its own and a row in the docs. A discussion is a contribution with `discussion`, the ids of GitHub's GraphQL API that its reply names: its draft is asked for as it comes (`askForDraft()` of `src/pager.ts`), and ✅ Send posts it as the app with `reply()` of `src/github.ts`, never in the maintainer's name. A discussion that GitHub dealt with, by a reply of the maintainer there, a marked answer, or closed or deleted, is the signal `discussion-done`, which makes its open thing `done`; a text of ✏️ Edit sets `ownDraft`, and from then on no draft of the control repository replaces it ([decision 0009](../docs/decisions/0009-a-discussion-that-github-dealt-with-is-done-and-an-own-draft-stays.md)). An issue or a pull request of someone else follows its comments the same way, with `comment` in place of `discussion`, which `answering()` of `src/store.ts` returns for both: a comment of someone else is the signal `comment`, which edits an open thing in place and notifies once per `QUIET` of `src/pager.ts`, and a comment of the maintainer, a closed issue and a closed pull request are `contribution-done`; `askForDraft()` sends the comment as `issueComment` ([decision 0011](../docs/decisions/0011-a-comment-on-an-issue-or-a-pull-request-edits-its-thing-and-notifies-once.md)). Nothing that an issue, a pull request or the control repository says runs: it is shown, escaped by `src/render.ts`.
- A workflow that fails on the default branch, any but those of a release, is a thing of the kind `workflow`, one per repository and workflow file (`keys.workflow()` of `src/store.ts`), from the signal `workflow` of `mainRun()` in `src/rules.ts`. `workflowFailed()` and `workflowPassed()` of `src/pager.ts` keep it: the failure of a first attempt waits unseen, with `snoozedUntil` as the end of `WAIT`, for the rerun of *After the checks*, and `settle()` of `src/workflows.ts` shows it from the schedule unless a rerun runs or passed; a run older than the one that the thing knows, by its id and attempt, changes nothing, and a pass ends it only when it ran the jobs that failed without one failing again. A job of GitHub Actions is no check of its own any more, and an issue of the bot-health bot is the signal `health`, which reads the run that it names ([decision 0014](../docs/decisions/0014-a-workflow-that-fails-on-main-pages-once-after-its-rerun.md)).
- `src/content.ts` reads what a thing says: `excerpt()` the start of the body of an issue, a pull request, a discussion or a comment, which the rules pass on and its message quotes, and `releaseNotes()` the notes in the body of a release pull request, after the mark of the blueprint's release-please. Both read the body as plain text, cut first and in linear loops, so no body can make the Worker slow; `src/render.ts` escapes and links what they keep and fits every message within the 4096 characters of Telegram (`MAX_MESSAGE`), and the start of a text never goes to the control repository (`unquoted()` of `src/topics.ts`).
- `src/translations.ts` shows the notes of a release in the language of the pager ([decision 0020](../docs/decisions/0020-the-notes-of-a-release-come-in-the-language-of-the-pager.md)): `heading()` words the headings of the kinds of change from the catalog (`notes.*` of `src/texts.ts`), and `askForTranslation()` of `src/pager.ts` sends the words of the items, without their scope, as `pager-translate` once per notes, by `notesKey()`, after the message went out in English. The body `translation` of `src/control.ts` edits the message in place, and `checked()` keeps the English of each line that lost a reference or a name of code, so the control repository can't make a message link less or name something else. A new heading of a kind of change takes its key in `HEADINGS` and in both catalogs; the record of a release keeps the translation, and a new head with the same notes carries it over.
- `src/pager.ts` turns signals into one message per thing, edited in place; `src/store.ts` keeps the state in Workers KV, without secrets. Mind the free plan of KV: write only when a thing changes. A record that an older pager kept is brought up to date as it is read, by `current()` of `src/store.ts`, never by a write of its own: so the entry of the social preview that a pager up to 0.8.1 kept under `issue:<number>` gets its mark `upload`, by its label, which keeps 🛠 Start fix away from it.
- `src/deliveries.ts` has GitHub deliver an event again whose answer failed, from the schedule, three attempts in all, and makes an event whose attempts all failed an entry of the alarm of the control repository ([decision 0012](../docs/decisions/0012-the-schedule-has-github-deliver-a-failed-event-again.md)). So **each signal must leave the same state when it comes twice**: a new kind of signal, or a change of one, takes its case in `each signal applied twice` of `test/deliveries.test.ts`. The schedule counts its calls to the network with `subrequests()` of the context, against the 50 of a request on the free plan of Workers, and the deliveries come last, with what the steps before them left.
- `src/tokens.ts` watches the tokens of the maintainer that expire: the token of Claude by `CLAUDE_TOKEN_EXPIRES`, `GITHUB_USER_TOKEN`, whose day the schedule reads once a day from the header `github-authentication-token-expiration` of `GET /rate_limit`, and `PAGER_FIX_TOKEN`, whose day the control repository sends as `tokens.fix`; each reminds three weeks before, as a `reminder` with its `token`. `src/health.ts` answers the signed body `health` of the workflow *Health* of the control repository, without a secret ([decision 0013](../docs/decisions/0013-the-control-repository-checks-the-health-of-the-pager-once-a-day.md)). Both keep their notes, the time of the schedule's last run and the days of the tokens, in the storage of the Durable Object (`local` of the context, a `Memory` in the tests), never in Workers KV, and never a token. A new check of the health is a field of its answer and a rule of `health.yml` in the control repository.
- The security of a repository comes in two kinds of things ([how it works](../docs/how-it-works.md#a-vulnerability-report-and-a-leaked-secret)). An alert of secret scanning is an entry of the security message of its repository, the bundle `alert` that it shares with code scanning, whose key starts with `SECRET_ENTRY` of `src/store.ts`; its file comes from `secretPath()` of `src/github.ts`, which reads the places of the alert and never the alert itself, whose answer holds the secret. A private vulnerability report is a thing of the kind `advisory`, under embargo until it is published: **never let its summary, its description or a secret reach a message, a record, a log, an answer to GitHub or the control repository**, as `test/security.test.ts` checks for every route; the rules read only its id, its severity and its day, and `src/advisories.ts`, the reminder of the schedule on the day before its acknowledgement is due, only its state, with `advisoryState()`.
- `src/topics.ts` gives each thing a topic of the chat: its first message opens it, its name gets ✅ once the thing is done, and a text in it goes to the control repository with the thing (`about()`). A topic that the maintainer deleted is done for him: `sendThing()` sends the next message of its thing into a new topic, and `postBelow()` sends every message below a thing's message, such as its pictures, the notice of a comment or a draft to read, which brings the thing's own message into a new topic first ([decision 0017](../docs/decisions/0017-a-topic-that-the-maintainer-deleted-opens-anew-with-the-next-message-of-its-thing.md)), and an album follows the message above it into its thread. A rename that Telegram refuses keeps the old name and marks the thing with `renameRefused`, which `put()` of `src/store.ts` writes into the metadata of its record, also of a done thing, and `renameAgain()` of `src/schedule.ts` tries it again for a day. Every other failure of a topic falls back to the main view, as before topics; the tests fake Telegram's topics with `withTopics()` of `test/helpers.ts`, a topic that the maintainer deleted with `withDeletedTopic()`, and a `Net` without them is a chat without topics.
- `src/texts.ts` holds every text that goes to the maintainer, one catalog per language, chosen by `LANGUAGE` in `wrangler.jsonc`: a new or changed text takes its entry in both catalogs, with the same placeholders, tags and emojis, as `test/texts.test.ts` checks. The rules return what they mean as a `Phrase` of that catalog, never words, and the logs stay in English.
- `src/control.ts` takes the signed answers of the private control repository: a draft, a note, a proposal with one ✅ Confirm button that carries the data of its thing's own button, and the end of a job that failed. The contract is in `docs/how-it-works.md`, and the workflow on the other side is in the public template `Dennis-Otto/repo-pager-control-template`, of which every control repository, the maintainer's private `Dennis-Otto/repo-pager-control` included, is a copy that takes its changes by a pull request of its workflow *Template* ([decision 0019](../docs/decisions/0019-the-control-repository-comes-from-a-public-template-which-every-copy-follows.md)): a change of the contract changes both, the Worker first, since it refuses a body that it doesn't know, then the template.
- A question of the maintainer's own agents is a thing of the kind `decision`, which `src/control.ts` makes from the body `ask` and whose buttons are its options (`choose` of `src/buttons.ts`); a press saves the answer as `answers/<id>.json` on the branch `pager-answers` of the control repository with `saveAnswer()` of `src/github.ts` ([decision 0008](../docs/decisions/0008-an-agent-reads-its-answer-from-a-branch-of-the-control-repository.md)), through `answerDecision()` of `src/actions.ts`, which a text in the topic of an open question also calls, with `choice` null and the text as its answer (`answerInWords()` of `src/updates.ts`); the body `withdraw` ends an open question without an answer ([decision 0010](../docs/decisions/0010-a-text-in-the-topic-of-a-question-answers-it-and-an-agent-may-take-it-back.md)). The body `report` keeps nothing: it is a message in a topic of its own, with `postInNewTopic()` of `src/topics.ts`.
- `src/pictures.ts` reads the artifacts of the visual check of a pull request, with the reader of ZIP files of `src/zip.ts`, and picks the album of its largest changes, each with the picture of its difference first when the artifact has one ([decision 0016](../docs/decisions/0016-the-album-of-a-visual-change-shows-the-changed-pixels-first.md)); a new form of report, name of artifact or key of a difference is taught there, with a test in `test/pictures.test.ts`, whose ZIP files come from `test/zips.ts`.
- The tests run in workerd against the simulated Telegram and GitHub of `test/helpers.ts`, which records each call; nothing goes to the network.
- The social preview, `.github/social-preview.html`, draws two messages of the pager in its chat: each text with `data-message` is exactly what `render()` of `src/render.ts` writes for a thing of `test/social-preview.test.ts`, without the addresses of its links, and each row of its keyboard what `keyboard()` of `src/buttons.ts` offers. A changed text, emoji or button of the pager makes that test fail: change the page with it, and the screenshot bot renders `.github/social-preview.png` anew, which then needs its upload under Settings → General → Social preview.
